label: copy phase, fed-back input is 2/u/p/1/n, from the 4th output onward
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original tokens or <DEL>). It needs the fed-back input (the previous output) to be one of a small token set: 2 (largest share of mass), u, p, 1, n. It is nearly silent before recall_idx 3, and the firing rate rises for longer sequences (L=9 holds 55% of the mass). The predicate covers 96% of activations and 98% of activation mass, but only about 1 in 5 predicted steps actually fires. Which output comes next modulates firing: rates are higher when the output is p/j/k/2/g/u/b, but restricting on this cut recall roughly in half (dev F1 0.46 vs 0.35). Also lower when the output is a digit or a vowel. I found no simple rule for which of the eligible steps fire. It does not fire on other input tokens (q, g, k, b and so on are under 0.5% each), and it does not fire in the original or delimiter phases.
